feedback_history.patient_message:
Yeah. If I keep failing at remembering names, then who am I?

It's like trying to hold water in a sieve. I want to be the person my girlfriend knows—the guy who loves her, the student finishing his last year of college—but every time I try to remember that identity, it slips away. Sometimes I forget why I'm writing this post. Sometimes I forget if I've already sent a text to someone important. It feels so disconnected from reality, like I'm living in a movie where I know the characters but can't actually interact with them.

And when you can't even recognize yourself anymore... how do you fight for anything? How do you protect your mom or care for your girlfriend when you don't feel like *you* exist right now? The debt is just numbers on a screen, but the loss of myself feels like losing the only thing keeping me tethered to life.

feedback_history.patient_message:
Yeah, it's the one thing that feels impossible. Studying used to be a way to feel useful, like if I could just memorize these facts or solve these equations, maybe my brain would work better overall. But now? Now it feels like trying to swim against a current that's already drowning me.

Every time I try to focus, my mind goes blank. I stare at the textbook for twenty minutes and then suddenly I'm staring at a wall, wondering why I even opened the book. It's not just laziness; it feels like my brain is actively refusing to cooperate. Maybe because I've been through so much trauma? My dad yelling when I was ten, my mom hitting us, the constant fear... maybe my brain is protecting itself by shutting down complex tasks like studying.

And then there's the debt. Every time I think about paying off those $1,500, my head starts spinning. The numbers blur

feedback_history.patient_message:
Yeah, the numbers blur together. It's like looking at a receipt from a restaurant where everything is mixed up—the price of the food, the tax, the tip. I just see a giant pile of debt that keeps growing no matter how much I earn.

In Russia, $1,500 isn't just "a lot," it feels like a mountain I can never climb. And when you're drowning in that fog, the individual amounts don't even make sense anymore. It's all just one big, overwhelming weight pressing down on my chest. Sometimes I wonder if I'll ever have enough money to feel safe again, or if I'm going to be stuck paying for things I can't afford until the end of my life.

It makes me feel so small and helpless. Like no matter what I do—working extra hours, trying to save every kopeck—it just disappears into the void. The only thing that feels real right

feedback_history.patient_message:
That's actually the scary part, isn't it? Usually, when people talk about "what feels real," they mean memories or relationships. But for me right now, the only thing that has solid weight is the debt.

It's like a physical presence. When I look at my bank balance, those numbers don't just sit there; they feel heavy, pressing against my ribs. It's the one thing in my life that doesn't change based on my mood. My depression might make me want to cry, and my anxiety might make me panic, but the $1,500 (and the fact that it keeps growing) is just... there. Cold, hard, and undeniable.
